title: Allocating Human Oversight in AI-Enabled Analytics
abstract: arXiv:2604.12497v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Artificial intelligence provides low-cost predictions for many analytics tasks, but their reliability and the value of another human label vary across tasks. We study how to allocate a shared human-validation budget when task-level uncertainty is unknown and each acquired label informs both estimation and subsequent allocation. For known difficulty levels, the benchmark follows a cost-adjusted Neyman rule that accounts for task importance and label cost. Within our Tuned Rectification-Difficulty framework, we develop an upper-confidence-bound policy that jointly learns the correction coefficients of tuned prediction-powered inference and the resulting difficulties from paired human labels and predictions, and establish an allocation-regret guarantee for the confidence-radius policy. translated_title: AI赋能分析中的人类监督分配
translated_abstract: 人工智能为许多分析任务提供了低成本的预测，但其可靠性以及额外获取一个人类标签的价值因任务而异。我们研究了在任务级不确定性未知的情况下，如何分配共享的人类验证预算，其中每个获取的标签同时服务于估计和后续的分配决策。对于难度已知的情形，基准方法遵循一种成本调整后的Neyman规则，该规则同时考虑任务重要性和标签成本。在我们的“调优纠偏-难度”框架内，我们开发了一种上置信界策略，从配对的人类标签和预测中联合学习调优预测驱动推断的校正系数以及由此产生的任务难度，并为置信半径策略建立了分配遗憾保证。在合成实验和一项包含68个任务、超过2000名受访者的真实数字孪生调查中，我们的方法弥补了与最优方案之间的大部分差距。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种在任务难度未知情形下分配共享人类验证预算的上置信界策略，能够从人类标签与AI预测的配对数据中联合学习预测校正系数和任务难度，并具有分配遗憾理论保证，在实验中将性能提升至接近最优方案的水平。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an upper-confidence-bound policy for allocating a shared human-validation budget under unknown task difficulty, which jointly learns the correction coefficients of tuned prediction-powered inference and task difficulties from paired human labels and predictions, with allocation-regret guarantees that close most of the gap to the oracle in experiments.
